installPrompt.iosBody: Tap the Share button, then choose 'Add to Home Screen'. It opens full screen, and records you save there open even without a connection. Records already saved in Safari stay in Safari.
about.scan.items.0: You get a clear yes or no, usually in about 10 seconds. A complex stacked sign can take longer.
about.evidence.items.2: Add a note about why you parked there (mum's hospital visit, Saturday market). It's kept with the record in your own words. Notes aren't signed.
about.sealCaveat: The seal shows the signed details existed, unchanged, by the time ParkProof signed them. It doesn't show they're true, that the AI read the sign correctly, who was driving, where the car was, or when it arrived or left.
about.gates.lead: Little checks for the conditions that are easy to miss, before you walk away.
about.gates.items.2: Parked somewhere with no signs at all? You can still log it, with a photo of the surroundings. The photo shows what was in view, not that there was no sign nearby.
about.appeal.lead: No need to start the dispute letter from scratch. We'll draft it for you to check and change.
about.appeal.items.1: You get a draft letter to the council to read and change before you send it. ParkProof doesn't rate your case or predict the outcome.
about.kindnesses.items.0: Free. No app store. Add it to your home screen and it works like a normal app. Your saved records open even without a connection, but checking a sign needs one.
landing.heroSubhead: Take a photo of any Aussie parking sign and get a clear, plain-English answer <accent>in seconds</accent>.
landing.evidenceCallout.body: Every parking record you save is signed, so anyone can check its details haven't changed since. A signature doesn't show they're true, who was driving, where the car was, or when it arrived or left.
active.recheckSub: Re-check now. See if you can still park here, in seconds.
scanner.privacyLine: To read the sign, we send the sign photo to an AI service. If you allow location, our server uses it to work out the local time. Reading the sign doesn't keep a copy of the photo on our servers. No account needed.
scanner.noSignChooseCopy: You can photograph the surroundings to show what was in view. The photo won't show there was no sign nearby.
scanner.noSignAmbientCaption: Taken to show the surroundings. It doesn't show there was no sign nearby.
result.firstSaveValue: Saving keeps a tamper-evident record of this park, in case you ever need it for a fine.
logger.intro: We'll save a record with the time, your photo and GPS, in case you ever need to dispute a fine.
logger.locationContext: We use your location only for this record. It's saved on this device, and backed up to the cloud only if you sign in.
logger.gpsImprecise: GPS is too rough to pin down your spot
logger.gpsImpreciseCopy: Reading is {{accuracy}}. That's fine for finding a coffee shop, but too rough to show which street you parked on. You can type the street address instead.
logger.gpsImpreciseDanger: Reading is {{accuracy}}, so it could even be the wrong suburb (common on Starlink, a VPN or indoors). You can type the street address instead.
logger.carOptionalHelp: Optional. It's saved with the record.

appeal.captureIntro: Take a photo of the infringement notice you received. Claude will read it, cross-reference it with the evidence saved in this record, and draft a formal letter you can send to the issuing council.
auth.signUpIntro: Sync records across devices, recover them if you lose your phone, and keep evidence safe even after you uninstall.
auth.footer: Cloud sync is optional. ParkProof works without an account, and your data lives on this device. Signing in just lets you see it on others.
settings.exportCopy: Downloads a PDF with every parking record you've stored in the cloud: a cover page summary, then each record's details with photos. Ready to print or share.
privacy.signingCopy: Signed in or not, each record is signed with an ECDSA P-256 key held in AWS KMS. To sign a record, ParkProof's server receives the details being signed (such as times, location, the sign reading, photo fingerprints and any names you enter, never the photos themselves) and sends back the signature. The private key never leaves AWS. The public key is published at /parkproof-public-key.pem so anyone (a council, court or insurer) can check the signatures with openssl dgst. A signature shows the signed details haven't changed since ParkProof signed them. It doesn't show they're true, who was driving, where the car was, or when the car arrived or left. The appendix in any exported PDF has the steps.

pdf.signature.intro: Each part of this record was signed by ParkProof's server when the server received it, at the signed_at time shown for that part. A valid signature shows the signed details and photo fingerprints have not changed since then. It does not show that they are true, who was driving, where the car was, or when the car arrived or left.
pdf.fullExport.intro: This document gathers every parking record saved to this ParkProof account, one section per record. Where a record has signed parts, its signature pages follow its section, with the steps to check each signature. A valid signature shows the signed details haven't changed since ParkProof signed them. It doesn't show that they are true, who was driving, where the car was, or when the car arrived or left.
about.lead: You probably came here thinking oh, it reads parking signs. It does. But while it's at it, we figured we'd also save the evidence in case you get a wrongful fine, draft a dispute letter for you to check if you do, and remind you to move your car before time runs out. Here's the friendly tour.
privacy.rightsAnonymous: If you don't sign in, your parking records are only on this device. Clear your browser storage to delete them. That doesn't delete what's already on our servers. A push reminder you set for a record is kept until it's sent or you cancel it. A weekly reminder by push is deleted within 90 days of the last time you opened ParkProof. This device's push registration (a random ID for this device, the push address and encryption keys your browser gave us, and when they were last renewed) is kept for about 90 days after ParkProof last renewed it. ParkProof renews it when you open the app with push reminders on and when you set a reminder. Switching push reminders off, in ParkProof or in your browser, doesn't tell our server, so the registration is kept as above. If the push service tells us the address no longer works (this can happen when a reminder you set earlier is sent after you switched them off), we delete the address and keys at once. We keep only this device's ID, a fingerprint of the address and when we found out, for about 90 days, so the address isn't stored again. Our server's logs also record this device's ID when it registers for push, sets a reminder or is sent one, with the push service it uses, the random ID of the record or weekly reminder, and when each reminder was set, sent or skipped. The logs are deleted after 90 days. Feedback you send, with your email if you add one, is kept for up to two years.
